items.claim: The unit is correctly bounded by the koh-amar frame onset at 66:1 and closes cleanly before the fresh imperative summons at 66:5, with SAMEKH corroboration on both sides and no undisclosed intervening tier-1 seam.
items.evidence: 66:1 opens with a verse-initial koh-amar frame (byte tier); 66:3's participial list ('one who slaughters an ox...') continues without any addressee shift or fresh frame marker, confirming there is no seam between the throne/footstool declaration and the sacrifice critique; 66:5 opens a fresh imperative addressed to a newly named audience ('those who tremble at his word'), a legitimate addressee-shift exit. SAMEKH marks at 65:25 (front) and 66:4 (close) corroborate both edges without conflict. The judgment_oracle unit_type call is defensible given the closing verdict-declaration, and the row's frontier-flag disclosure of the poor/contrite-vs-sacrifice-critique tension is confined to content interpretation, not the boundary warrant.

items.claim: The imperative-summons unit is correctly bounded from 66:5's fresh addressee-directed onset through 66:9's SAMEKH-marked close, with the following imperative at 66:10 confirming the exit seam.
items.evidence: 66:5 opens with a verse-initial imperative addressed to 'those who tremble', distinct from the preceding unit's frame; the birth-of-Zion material (66:7-9) is presented as the content of that same summons with no intervening frame marker; 66:10 opens its own fresh imperative to a differently named audience. SAMEKH marks at 66:4 (front) and 66:9 (close) corroborate both edges. The salvation_oracle unit_type call is properly disclosed given the embedded vindication/judgment material at the unit's opening.

items.claim: The two-verse rejoice-summons is correctly retained as its own unit, doubly bracketed by SAMEKH marks and by a fresh imperative onset at front / fresh koh-amar reopening at rear, and the rejected merge-forward alternative is fairly stated and properly declined.
items.evidence: 66:10 opens a fresh imperative to a newly named audience (those who love/mourn over Jerusalem), distinct in both addressee and grammatical person from the preceding unit; 66:12 reopens an explicit koh-amar frame, a legitimate frame shift from the human-addressed imperative of 66:10-11. SAMEKH marks at 66:9 (front) and 66:11 (close) corroborate both edges without conflict.
tier_citations: byte tier: oshb:Isa.66.10 (imperative onset); oshb:Isa.66.12 (koh-amar onset)

items.claim: The comfort oracle is correctly bounded by the koh-amar reopening at 66:12 and the theophany-onset shift at 66:15, and the rejected alternative (that 66:14's close belongs to the following judgment unit) is properly declined on person/register grounds.
items.evidence: 66:12 opens a fresh koh-amar frame, distinct from the preceding imperative unit; 66:14's closing clause remains third-person report continuing that same divine-speech frame ('his servants'/'his enemies'), not a fresh vocative or frame marker. 66:15's theophany-announcement idiom (כִּֽי הִנֵּ֤ה יְהוָה֙ בָּאֵ֣שׁ...) recurs byte-identically at only one other site in the book (כִּֽי הִנֵּ֤ה יְהוָה֙ יֹצֵ֣א... at 26:21), supporting its function as a genuine two-site recurring onset formula rather than a bare thematic label, even though the row's own prose frames the exit only in register terms ('a different register'). SAMEKH at 66:11 (front) corroborates; the row correctly discloses that no mark falls at the unit's own close.
tier_citations: skeleton tier: the theophany idiom recurs at oshb:Isa.26.21 and oshb:Isa.66.15 only (2-site sweep)

items.claim: The theophany-judgment unit is correctly bounded by the formulaic 'behold, Yahweh will come' onset at 66:15 (a genuine two-site recurring idiom, not a bare thematic label) and the divine-speech/neum closure at 66:17, with the exit to 66:18 grounded in an actual grammatical person shift that the row's 'first-person emphatic pivot' language correctly identifies without naming the underlying mechanism.
items.evidence: The theophany idiom (כִּֽי הִנֵּ֤ה יְהוָה֙ בָּאֵ֣שׁ...) recurs at exactly two sites in the book, 26:21 and 66:15, making the 66:15 onset a byte-checkable recurring device rather than a purely content-based register call. 66:16-17 remain third-person report about Yahweh/the offenders through the neum-Yahweh closing tag; 66:18 opens with the emphatic first-person pronoun (וְאָנֹכִ֗י), a genuine voice shift from third-person report to first-person divine address. The ketiv/qere note at 66:17 is correctly disclosed as single-witness and non-adjudicated; no petuchah/setumah mark falls in this span, correctly disclosed as absent.
tier_citations: skeleton tier: the theophany idiom recurs at oshb:Isa.26.21 and oshb:Isa.66.15 only (2-site sweep)

items.claim: The unit's own boundaries (66:18-66:22) are well-warranted by the first-person voice shift at 66:18 and the neum closure within 66:22, but the device_notes mischaracterizes the 65:17/66:22 'new heavens and new earth' relationship as a skeleton-tier recurrence when a direct collation of the two phrasings returns no match at any tier.
items.evidence: 65:17's phrase (skeleton: כי הנני בורא שמים חדשים וא..., an indefinite, bare noun-adjective construction) and 66:22's phrase (skeleton: כי כאשר השמים החדשים והארץ החדש..., a definite construction with the article prefixed to both noun and adjective) differ at the consonantal-skeleton level because of this definite-article morphology; collating the 66:22 phrase directly against the 65:17 verse returns no tier match at all (not skeleton, not accent-stripped, not nfd). The relationship is a shared-root lexical echo, not a verified skeleton-tier recurrence, and the row's observed_substrate_signals tag borrows the refrain-device namespace for what direct collation shows to be a looser echo than that label and the device_notes wording imply. This does not touch the row's actual boundary warrant, since the echo is already disclosed in the row's own evidence list as not a boundary driver -- the defect is confined to tier-precision in a non-driving corroboration note.
tier_citations: byte tier: oshb:Isa.66.22 (row's own quote, confirmed byte)
direct collation of the 66:22 new-heavens/new-earth phrase against oshb:Isa.65.17 returns tier: none

items.claim: The book's closing couplet is correctly held as its own unit at reduced (medium_low) confidence with the coda-vs-close crux properly disclosed and not adjudicated, and the unmarked front-seam at 66:22 is honestly disclosed rather than treated as corroboration.
items.evidence: 66:23 opens with a recurring-liturgical 'month by month, sabbath by sabbath' formula, a tense/content shift from the one-time ingathering narrative of the preceding unit to iterative cultic practice; 66:22's comparative clause gives no tier-1 onset of its own, so the row correctly does not overclaim mark corroboration at that seam (no petuchah/setumah mark falls at 66:22-66:24, confirmed absent from the disclosure inventory). The closing image (66:24, the unburied transgressors) is held terminal by virtue of being the book's last verse, and the row properly declines to adjudicate whether it functions as this oracle's own close or a coda to the whole book.
